SATOM 2.13.0

SATOM learns what each firmware build really supports, over both the REST API and the CLI, and uses it to check every write, predict whether a configuration survives an upgrade, and write fields only the CLI can set.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user

Released: 2026-10-07 · All releases

In short#

2.13.0 is about firmware builds. SATOM now reads what each build of an appliance offers through both channels — the REST API it already used, and the appliance's own command line — and keeps that knowledge per build. On top of it come four things you can use: a Build compatibility check on every write and a page to explore it, a Migration Report that tells you whether an appliance's configuration will survive a move to another build, a CLI writer for the fields only the command line can set, and a new-build watch that warns administrators when an appliance runs a build SATOM has not studied yet.

The release also extends vendor release notes to FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer and FortiGate, ships a knowledge pack with the release, and records the firmware build on every WAF exception.

What's new#

Build compatibility on every write#

Before SATOM writes to an appliance, it now checks the change against that appliance's exact firmware build:

  • Fields the build does not have are removed for that device and listed, for example "Applies, but on 8.0.6 this field does not exist: it will be skipped on 3 appliances". When SATOM knows the field's new name, it says so.
  • Fields that only the command line can set are flagged, because a REST write cannot set them.
  • A value outside the allowed options or range, or an object the build does not have, blocks the write.
  • A build SATOM has never measured reads "not measured — cannot be guaranteed". It is never reported as fine.

The check runs in template apply and the automatic deploy after an approval, baseline and system profile apply (devices that cannot take a field are skipped one by one in bulk runs), the exception push and the object editor (a dry run shows it; a real write with an invalid value is refused).

The Build compatibility page#

A new Build compatibility page, reached from the API library, shows:

  • a field × build matrix that says for each field whether a build serves it over both channels, the CLI only, hidden in the full configuration only, REST only, or is unknown — with filters and paging;
  • a comparison of two builds: objects and fields added and removed, changed options, types, ranges and defaults, rename candidates and fields that moved;
  • the history of one field across builds.

See Build compatibility.

Migration Report: will this configuration survive build X?#

The new Migration Report page (Automation, next to Upgrade Flow; also reachable from the appliance page) answers one question before an upgrade. You pick an appliance and a target build; SATOM takes the appliance's newest full configuration from the backup vault (or a backup you choose) and checks every object and field it uses against the target build.

Each finding is classified:

  • Block — an object or field the device uses is removed, a value is no longer accepted, a value is out of range, or a type change the value does not satisfy.
  • Translate — a rename your field mappings already cover.
  • Warn — a likely rename, a changed default under a field left at its default, no evidence for the target, or a target build that is only partly measured (with its percentage).
  • Info — new objects and fields, with their default when known.

The verdict is ready, ready with warnings, blocked or cannot assess. The same build means nothing to do, and a downgrade gets the same checks. You can export the report as JSON or CSV. Configuration values stay in memory: the report and its exports carry names, counts and library facts only. The page uses the same permission as Upgrade Flow.

Upgrade Flow stage 1 now shows the migration verdict for each appliance's planned move, with a link to the full report (up to 20 appliances per page; the rest link to the report). See Migration report.

CLI writer: fields only the CLI serves#

Some fields can only be set from the appliance's command line. The object editor now handles them:

  • Each field of a save is routed by what the appliance's exact build supports: CLI-only and hidden fields go through the command line, the others through REST as before. A field the build does not have, or one SATOM never measured, is refused with the reason.
  • The Save preview shows the CLI script for the command-line part next to the usual REST request.
  • The change to one object runs as a single CLI transaction. SATOM stops at the first error the appliance prints and cancels the pending change, so nothing half-done is left behind.
  • After Apply, SATOM opens a fresh session and reads the object back over the CLI (and over REST when it can). Every written field must read back equal, or the write fails and shows the difference. After a failure, the read-back proves whether anything was applied.
  • Every apply is audited with the object and field names and the outcome, never the values.
  • It uses the same permission as before, the same per-device lock as a REST write, and dry run stays the default.

On FortiWeb 7.6.8 and 8.0.6 no field is CLI-only, so on those builds every field still goes through REST. This was tested end to end on a FortiWeb 8.0.6 lab appliance. See CLI writer.

Harvest the CLI schema of a build#

The API library now also learns from the appliance's command line: the full command tree of the running build (objects, fields, types, options) and the field names its full configuration shows, hidden ones included. Only names are collected, never values. You start it with Harvest CLI schema in the API Explorer (it runs as a device job and only reads from the appliance), from a scheduled action, or from the operator CLI. Comparing two builds now also covers the CLI side: fields that changed channel, options added and removed, type and range changes, and rename candidates — which are reported but never applied.

Schema builds page and the new-build watch#

  • When an appliance runs a build SATOM has no schema for, administrators get one bell notification per product and build: "New build X on Y: schema not harvested". It comes from the firmware check and from a new scheduled action.
  • The new Schema builds page (sidebar) lists each product's schema reader and whether it has been verified, the builds waiting to be harvested with a one-click harvest, and — after a harvest — what is new or changed compared with the closest known build, marked "to verify" where the REST side is not yet measured.
  • Schema reading now works per product. FortiWeb, FortiAuthenticator and FortiGate are verified on real appliances; FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer are supported but not yet verified on a real device.

See Schema builds.

A knowledge pack ships with each release#

Next to the release packs, each release now carries one knowledge pack built by the separate SATOM Harvester tool and signed with the release key.

  • Installing or updating SATOM imports every pending shipped pack: the newest release pack, then the newest knowledge pack, each only if this node has not fully imported it yet. Older packs of the same series are superseded and skipped.
  • A run with a failed item, or where you imported only some items, leaves the pack pending, so the next update tries again. The import history now records such runs as partial.
  • Software Update lists knowledge packs with the label knowledge pack (satom-harvester), marks superseded packs, and the pending notice names every pending pack.

See API library and API packs and The Knowledge Harvester.

Release notes for FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer and FortiGate#

  • Release notes now cover FortiAuthenticator (6.6 and 8.0), FortiAnalyzer and FortiGate. Their special notices feed the upgrade notes the advisor reads.
  • The Release Notes window is offered in the FortiAuthenticator and FortiAnalyzer workspaces too. FortiGate notes travel in API packs.
  • A build your appliances run that has no notes on this node is listed in the version pickers. Picking it while the vendor's website is unreachable says "No release notes for this build (offline: import a newer API pack)" instead of showing an empty list.

See Release notes.

Exceptions remember their firmware build#

  • Every WAF and signature exception, and its fleet library copy, now records the firmware build and REST API version it was written for. Copies on other appliances keep the original build; editing the content updates it; rollback and restore bring back the build of the old version. No existing history gains an extra version because of this.
  • Inject to device and the Attack ID insert check the exception against the target's build with the same rules as templates: discarded, renamed or unsupported fields block the push. An approver can override with a reason, and the override is audited. Exception details are not measured yet, so most pushes show "no evidence" — a warning, never a pass.
  • Line profiles show the build of each line's protection template and the builds its approval covers. The new-policy wizard warns, without blocking, when that template does not fit or was never validated for the device's build.

See Exceptions & Signature carve-outs and Line profiles.

What changes for you#

  • The CLI-coverage badges are more honest. Many blocks marked "CLI only" are in fact served by REST and just missing from the catalog. A block SATOM measured as served is now a catalog gap; the others read Not in catalog, and the REST column says CLI only only when REST was measured absent.
  • The release-notes scan lost its Firecrawl option. The endpoint and key fields and the "Direct" switch are gone from the scan panel; the scan only downloads directly from the vendor. A node without Internet gets the same notes from an API pack. An old browser tab or script that still sends those fields is not refused; the fields are ignored.
  • Every sidebar row is the same size. Nested FortiWeb rows used smaller text and shorter rows, the Global workspace links sat slightly out of line, and some sub-menu headings were shifted left. All rows now match; depth is shown by the indent only.

Fixed#

  • Build compatibility in the Global workspace answered with an error page. It now opens.
  • False "CLI only" fields. On a node where a table was empty, the channel view could mark hundreds of fields "CLI only" just because the vendor documentation did not list them (242 on FortiWeb 7.6.8). Only a real measurement can now say a field is missing; documentation alone leaves it unknown.
  • Lab evidence from knowledge packs was skipped when the node had measured the same build itself, so tables that are empty in production stayed unknown. Lab evidence is now imported alongside your own; it can only add, never replace.
  • False "REST only" fields. Internal bookkeeping fields such as row numbers were classed as REST-only. They are now set apart and no longer count against completeness; on the lab pack FortiWeb 7.6.8 went from 276 REST-only fields to none. Fields the documentation names but the appliance contradicts are marked unknown with a conflict note.
  • Object renames between builds were missed. Comparing FortiWeb 7.6.8 with 8.0.6 now reports the rename of the allowed source IP object to the source IP list, and the fields that moved.
  • FortiWeb paths that are not really served. FortiWeb answers some nested addresses it does not serve with its parent's data. Discovery took those answers as real and could register endpoints that only ever returned their parent. They are now recognised as absent; a real empty table still counts as served.
  • FortiGate schema reading was checked against a live FortiOS 8.0.1 appliance: display-only helpers are no longer counted as REST fields, nested object members are compared on both channels, and tables that only REST serves now show as REST-only.
  • Command tree reading: a prompt stuck to the first line no longer blanks it (one appliance lost an object, another gained phantom ones), and FortiOS field names that contain a space are read whole.
  • Full configuration reading: a value containing an escaped quote no longer swallows the lines after it.
  • Release notes scans found nothing. The vendor's documentation site changed its page layout and every scan ended in "no release notes found". The new layout is read now.
  • Known issues were cut short. FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer split their known-issue lists into one table per category and only the first was read (8 of 66 for FortiGate 7.6.4). Every table is read now.
  • Software Update failed to sort pack versions as soon as a knowledge pack sat next to release packs. It sorts them correctly now.

Under the hood#

  • The API library stores both channels per build and keeps the REST-only pages (versions page, preflights, baselines, matrix export) reading REST evidence only.
  • The command used to read the CLI tree is allowed only as an exact match behind its own safeguard; the read-only console rules are unchanged.
  • API packs carry the new CLI evidence, and a row carrying a configuration value is refused both at export and at import.
  • An unused Web Protection side menu that was rebuilt on every request was removed; the visible sidebar is unchanged.
